title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The dirty guard fires on a freshly opened theme nobody touched
detail: "The dirty guard 'save changes before...' always fires, even on a newly opened theme that I haven't touched the artboard. Something must be polluting its save data, maybe the telemetry data is leaking?" CAUSE ESTABLISHED: two exports six seconds apart differ only in scene.objects.{17,18,44}.styles. removeRuntimeText rewrites a sampled reading's text to an em-dash but not Fabric's per-character styles array, which is not in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES. A reading that changes length moves the spans, the serialised scene moves, the key moves. The user was right about the source and wrong about the mechanism. WANTS A SPEC, not a patch — see docs/product/../superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md for the adjacent question.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: Asset handling: the layer list is inconsistent, and some assets cannot be removed
detail: DEFECT 1 IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT; the rest is still open. The row claimed Replace allocates a new path per import so it cannot be pointing at what it replaces, and that was the cleanest cause and would have gone first. It does not happen: with a PNG selected in the assets dropdown, replacing it with a different PNG left the list at two entries and kept the same key, so Replace replaces in place and the key an author sees does not move. A second thing measured in the same sitting and NOT a defect: Replace refuses a file of a different extension with the message A replacement must keep the asset file extension, which is the right refusal and is already specific about the reason. NOT ESTABLISHED, and the row should say so rather than let the refutation read as a fix: I did not confirm the replaced assets BYTES changed, because the package round-trip needed to read them did not complete — Release package prompts for a version bump and Save package did not fire a download in that state — and an imported asset does not survive a reload unsaved, so the preview cannot stand in for it. Defects 2 and 3 (the layer list is inconsistent; some assets show as layers and some do not) and 4 (some assets cannot be removed, which waits on vg-034) remain unmeasured. This is also issue #14 in one example, and vg-047 was folded into this row as its duplicate.

title: A colour picker for paint
detail: The editor has no colour affordance at all; the palette manager's only control is free text. THE SEARCH ANSWERED THE WRONG ECOSYSTEM: @base-ui/react ships no colour picker, which is true and beside the point — the standing intent is Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind, and shadcn/ui has one. The alpha trap still binds: panel is #081523d9 at 85% and frost at 30%, so a bare input[type=color] cannot represent the part that matters.

title: A gradient editor sharing the colour picker's parts
detail: The palette accepts gradients — the Paint chooser offers Linear gradient, the manager has an angle and a stop list — but the stops are text fields. The reuse answer is that the colour picker's swatch and stop list already ARE the gradient editor: a solid is a single stop. Blocked behind vg-031.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail: The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.
